headline: 17 contracts catalogued across Ethereum-side gateway infrastructure; 5 proxy contracts with upgrade history confirmed on-chain; admin role holders (multisigs) referenced in audit but specific addresses and thresholds not yet on-chain-confirmed.

findings.text: Etherscan name-tag 'Sonic Labs: Sonic Gateway' found at 0xa1E2481a9CD0Cb0447EeB1cbc26F1b3fff3bec20 (TokenDeposit proxy) with implementation 0xAdE2eF0101278fe11490F2EE2aaD7915a094ADe9 (upgraded 2025-04-17). ValidatorsRegistry at 0x72965045A6691E5A74299D1e878f303264D4D910 surfaced from search. 3 proxy upgrades visible on Etherscan history.

Official deployed contracts page at https://docs.soniclabs.com/sonic/build-on-sonic/contract-addresses lists 8 Ethereum-side Gateway contracts: MPTProofVerifier, StateOracle, ValidatorsRegistry, TokenPairs (proxy+impl), TokenDeposit (proxy+impl), DirectExitAdministrator, UpdateManager (proxy+impl). All addresses recorded.

OpenZeppelin audit (Dec 13, 2024) of Fantom-foundation/Bridge at commit 558465d covers 13 Solidity contracts and off-chain Go relay/voter components. Audit identifies multisig admin roles on Bridge, ExitAdministrator, TokenPairs, UpdateManager, and TokenDeposit contracts, but specific multisig addresses are not published in the audit. Audit resolved 1 high, 1 of 3 mediums.

GitHub repo https://github.com/Fantom-foundation/Bridge referenced in OpenZeppelin audit at commit 558465d. Repo was not directly fetched (not pre-approved URL). Commit SHA 558465d captured from fetched audit page. No deployment artifact JSONs could be read without fetching.

protocol.chains lists only Ethereum; no multi-chain enumeration required. Sonic-side contracts (Bridge, TokenPairs, StateOracle, MPTProofVerifier, ValidatorsRegistry, MessageBus, UpdateManager on Sonic) are out-of-scope for this Ethereum-only run but recorded in admin_addresses for completeness.
TokenPairs contract at 0xf2b1510c2709072C88C5b14db90Ec3b6297193e4 is a token-pair registry (originalToMinted mapping), not a pool factory. No factory-child enumeration required. No cap notice needed.

Role taxonomy applied: TokenDeposit=vault (fund-holding ERC1967 proxy); UpdateManager=admin (central upgrade controller, proxy); ValidatorsRegistry=other (verifier, owned by UpdateManager); StateOracle=oracle; MPTProofVerifier=other; TokenPairs=other (registry, proxy); DirectExitAdministrator=guardian (failsafe withdrawals). All admin multisig actors listed as actor_class=unknown pending on-chain owner reads.

All addresses in admin_addresses trace to the fetched docs.soniclabs.com page or the fetched Etherscan page. Implementation address 0xAdE2eF0101278fe11490F2EE2aaD7915a094ADe9 traces to fetched Etherscan proxy upgrade history. Multisig owners referenced in OZ audit but no specific multisig addresses appear in either fetched source — not included in admin_addresses.

rationale.verdict: Discovery run walked three corpora: the official docs page (fetched, 8 Ethereum-side addresses recovered), Etherscan for the primary contract (fetched, upgrade history and current implementation confirmed), and the OpenZeppelin audit page (fetched, scope and privileged-role structure documented). 17 total contracts catalogued (8 Ethereum-side gateway + 7 Sonic-side out-of-scope + 2 additional implementations from Etherscan upgrade history). Key gap: multisig addresses holding DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE on UpdateManager, ExitAdministrator, TokenPairs, and TokenDeposit are not published in any fetched source; these must be discovered via on-chain owner/getRoleMember calls in the next assessment run.

admin_addresses.role: vault (TokenDeposit proxy — ERC1967, holds bridged ERC-20 tokens)
admin (UpdateManager proxy — central parameter and contract upgrade controller)
guardian (DirectExitAdministrator — failsafe withdrawal for bridge-dead scenario)
oracle (StateOracle — stores Merkle root of Sonic state; updated by UpdateManager)
other (ValidatorsRegistry — owned by UpdateManager, stores validator set and weights)
other (TokenPairs proxy — registry mapping Ethereum ERC-20 to Sonic minted tokens)

protocol_metadata.about: Sonic Gateway is the native canonical bridge enabling ERC-20 token transfers between Ethereum and the Sonic Layer-1 blockchain. Users deposit tokens into the TokenDeposit contract on Ethereum, which locks them; an off-chain IBC relay network of Sonic validators then updates a Merkle root in each chain's StateOracle, allowing the recipient to prove the deposit and claim bridged (minted) IOU tokens on Sonic. The bridge uses a 'dead bridge' failsafe mechanism: if Sonic is inactive for more than 14 days, users can recover locked assets on Ethereum via the DirectExitAdministrator. Core Ethereum-side contracts (TokenDeposit, UpdateManager, TokenPairs) are ERC1967 upgradeable proxies; critical admin roles are held by multisigs whose addresses and thresholds have not been publicly disclosed.
